workflow: Manually updating dependencies across multiple repositories by creating pull requests for each package update
trigger: New version release of a dependency or security advisory
current_workaround: Using Dependabot or Renovate bot, but manually reviewing and merging each PR; often resorting to local scripts or manual git commands
consequence: Delayed security patches, outdated dependencies, breaking changes missed, maintainer burnout

workflow: Copying and modifying CI/CD pipeline configuration files (e.g., GitHub Actions YAML) for each new environment (dev, staging, prod) and each microservice
trigger: Adding a new service or environment
frequency: Per new service or environment (weekly to monthly)
current_workaround: Manually duplicating workflow files, using environment variables, or templating with tools like copier or cookiecutter
consequence: Configuration drift, hard-to-debug build failures, time wasted on repetitive edits, increased risk of misconfiguration

workflow: Using GitHub Issues as a makeshift code review tracking system because the built-in review workflow doesn't support custom checklists, approval gates, or cross-repo reviews
trigger: Starting a pull request that requires additional review steps beyond the standard GitHub review
current_workaround: Creating issues linked to PRs, manually tracking review status in spreadsheets, or using external tools like Asana or Jira
consequence: Lost context, duplicate work, missed review deadlines, low visibility into review pipeline
